questions.question: How does a family most often get money?
options: From adults working - salary or wages
questions.explanation: A family most often gets money from the work of adults. When parents work, they receive a salary or payment for their work.

questions.question: Chrumko notices that mom is looking at a message on her phone from the bank. What happened?
options: Mom received her paycheck from work
questions.explanation: Mom received her paycheck - money she gets for her work. This money arrives in her bank account.

questions.question: What is this money used for?
options: For rent, groceries, school supplies and more
questions.explanation: This money is used for rent, groceries and school supplies. It finances everything the family needs.

questions.question: The money in a household comes because parents work and receive payment for their work.
questions.explanation: Work by adults is the primary source of money for a family.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Parents receive a salary for their work.
Money in a family comes from various sources.
questions.explanation: Money doesn't appear on its own - it must be earned through work.

questions.question: Match the source of money with the correct description.
questions.explanation: There are several ways a family can have money resources, but work is the most common.

questions.question: Place each item in the correct category: How money is used.
questions.explanation: Money is used first for needs, then for things we want.

questions.question: Put in order what Chrumko realizes about money in the family.
orderItems: Mom gets a message from the bank about her paycheck
Chrumko understands that household money comes from work
Chrumko sees how money is used for rent and groceries
questions.explanation: Chrumko gradually understands the relationship between work and money in the family.

questions.question: What are household expenses?
options: All the money that needs to be paid for the home to function
questions.explanation: Household expenses are all the money that needs to be paid for the home to function - housing, food, water, electricity, transportation, etc.

questions.question: Chrumko wonders why his parents didn't buy a decorative flowerpot this month that they liked. What does father say?
options: We had to pay the internet, water and other necessary bills
questions.explanation: Father tells him they had to pay the internet, water and other necessary bills. Even though these aren't big things, together they add up to a large sum.

questions.question: All the money a family earns is spent only on luxury and entertainment.
questions.explanation: Most of the money is spent on necessary expenses like rent, groceries and energy.

questions.question: Match each expense with its category.
questions.explanation: Necessary expenses are for household functioning, free expenses are for entertainment.

questions.question: Place household expenses in the correct groups.
questions.explanation: A family must budget so they have enough for necessary expenses.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Household expenses include rent, water and electricity.
Money often goes to many small necessary payments.
Households don't have to pay for water because it's just a natural thing.
questions.explanation: Water must be brought to the house and that costs money.

questions.question: Why are internet and water bills important expenses?
options: Because they're services needed for safety and communication in the family
questions.explanation: Services like water and internet are essential for family health and education.

questions.question: Why do we pay for housing even though we live in it?
options: Housing requires care, maintenance and services that cost money
questions.explanation: We pay for housing through rent, mortgage or fees associated with living. This also includes services like water, heating and waste removal.

questions.question: A home needs care and maintenance, which means new expenses can appear.
questions.explanation: When something breaks, it needs to be fixed, which costs money.

questions.question: Match each housing-related expense with its correct description.
questions.explanation: Some expenses are regular (rent, heating), others are unexpected (repairs).

questions.question: Place items in the correct groups of housing expenses.
questions.explanation: A family must plan and save money for unexpected repairs too.

questions.question: Chrumko's mom says the roof needs to be fixed. What happens?
options: Fixing the roof is an unexpected but necessary expense
questions.explanation: When a home breaks, it needs to be fixed to be safe - these are unexpected but necessary expenses.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Rent is a monthly expense for housing.
Repairs and home maintenance are unexpected expenses that will never happen.
Heating is a necessary expense in winter.
questions.explanation: Repairs will have to be done - homes require maintenance.

questions.question: Put in order how Chrumko learns about housing costs.
orderItems: Chrumko sees his parents paying rent
Mom explains to him that housing is more than just a space
Chrumko sees something break and it needs to be fixed
Chrumko understands that housing costs money and requires care
questions.explanation: Gradually Chrumko understands the complexity of housing expenses.

questions.question: Why doesn't the refrigerator fill itself with food?
options: Food gets used up and needs to be bought regularly
questions.explanation: Food is one of the regular expenses. Groceries get consumed and need to be purchased frequently.

questions.question: Chrumko goes grocery shopping with mom. What do they buy?
options: Bread, milk, fruit, cheese, pasta and yogurt
questions.explanation: They put bread, milk, fruit, cheese, pasta and yogurt in the cart. It seems like they're only buying a few things.

questions.question: Food is a regular large part of family expenses.
questions.explanation: Every family must regularly buy groceries, which is one of the largest expenses.

questions.question: Match each food item with its expense category.
questions.explanation: Basic groceries are needs, while candy is free spending.

questions.question: Place each food item in the correct category.
questions.explanation: The budget should prioritize basic groceries over sweets.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Food gets used up and needs to be bought regularly.
Food is a large part of family expenses.
A family should spend all their money on candy, not on basic groceries.
questions.explanation: Basic groceries are a necessity, candy is only sometimes, if money is left.

questions.question: Why is it important to plan grocery shopping?
options: Because it's good to know how much money is spent
Because we might need different groceries at different times
questions.explanation: Planned shopping helps save money and ensures the family has enough food.

questions.question: Why do parents turn off lights even though they could leave them on longer?
options: Because electricity, water and heating cost money
questions.explanation: Electricity, water and heating are services that the family pays regular bills for. The more energy used, the higher the bill can be.

questions.question: Chrumko leaves his room and leaves the light on. What does mom do?
options: Calls Chrumko back and asks him to turn it off
questions.explanation: Mom calls him back and asks him to turn off the light. She explains that small things add up over the course of a month.

questions.question: Energy isn't visible as a physical thing, but it costs money every day.
questions.explanation: Electricity, water and gas are invisible, but their consumption is paid in monthly bills.

questions.question: Match each action with the correct effect on energy costs.
matchLeft: Leaving the fridge open for long
questions.explanation: All these actions affect the household budget.

questions.question: Sort activities by how they affect energy consumption.
questions.explanation: Small habits over time contribute to larger savings or costs.

questions.question: One of these statements is wrong. Find it.
options: Electricity, water and heating are services that must be paid for.
Small things like repeatedly turning off lights add up over the month.
Energy is free and we don't need to worry about it.
questions.explanation: Energy must be paid for and its consumption accumulates over the month.

questions.question: Put in order how Chrumko learns that energy costs money.
orderItems: Mom explains to him that electricity costs money
Chrumko sees the monthly energy bill
Chrumko realizes that saving energy saves money for the family
questions.explanation: Gradually he understands the cumulative effect of energy consumption.

questions.question: How can all family members help reduce energy expenses?
options: Turn off lights when leaving a room
Turn off water while brushing teeth
questions.explanation: All family members have a role in saving energy and water.
